Ramenhead is Cape Town's home of authentic Japanese ramen — a casual, walk-in ramen-ya in the heart of the city at Speaker's Corner, 37 Parliament Street. Every bowl begins with noodles made fresh in-house on the only Yamato noodle machine in Africa, paired with broths simmered for 48 hours until they carry real umami depth.

Behind the pass: Executive Chef Julia du Toit, with guidance from FYN Group's Peter Tempelhoff and Ashley Moss. The kitchen takes its cue from the ramen shops of Japan, building each bowl with authentic technique — and extending the same care to small plates, gyoza, and Japanese street food like okonomiyaki fries and chicken karaage. The bar pours sake from traditional masu cups, award-winning Japanese-inspired cocktails, and local and imported beers.

Open Tuesday through Saturday from 5 PM, with happy hour weekdays 5–7 PM (50% off all small plates and selected cocktails) and live music every Thursday. Walk-ins welcome; book a table via Dineplan. Outside seating available, weather dependent. No cash payments.

item.title: Eat Out: FYN's Team to Open a Casual Ramen House in Cape Town
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
South Africa's leading restaurant publication, Eat Out, was first to break the story that the team behind award-winning FYN — chefs Peter Tempelhoff and Ashley Moss — were preparing to launch Ramenhead, a casual, fast-paced ramen house in the heart of Cape Town. The feature introduced what would become Cape Town's home of authentic Japanese ramen: silky, freshly-made noodles, slow-simmered broths and izakaya-style small plates served in a buzzing, walk-in-friendly setting at Speaker's Corner.

The Eat Out piece set expectations early. Ramenhead would carry the same uncompromising kitchen standards as its acclaimed sibling FYN — celebrated among The World's 50 Best Restaurants — but in a relaxed, after-work format. Readers got a first look at a noodle bar built around real Japanese technique, plated with the precision of a fine-dining team. For Cape Town's food scene, the announcement signalled the arrival of a serious new ramen destination rather than just another casual opening.

Source: Eat Out
